items.prompt: A tampered browser posts a new invoice whose total field is far below the sum of its items. Which total is stored?
items.answer: The total the controller recomputes from the line items
distractors: The client total, since Joi accepted the field as a number
The lower of the two totals, to protect the paying client
Neither one; the save fails a Mongoose total validator
items.explanation: invoiceController/create.js recomputes every item total, subTotal, taxTotal and total with calculate and writes them over body before saving, so a client-sent total stops mattering.

items.prompt: A script bypasses the UI and posts a payment larger than the invoice's remaining balance. What does paymentController/create.js send back?
items.answer: A 202 with success: false and the maximum amount allowed
distractors: A 400 from the payment Joi schema, before any lookup runs
A 200, after which the invoice credit exceeds its total
A 409 conflict, because the credit would pass the total
items.explanation: The controller reloads the invoice, computes maxAmount = total - discount - credit and, if amount > maxAmount, returns status 202 with success: false and "The Max Amount you can add is ...". The client-side maxAmount in RecordPayment.jsx is only for UX.

items.prompt: The Node process dies after Payment.create succeeds but before the Invoice.findOneAndUpdate runs. What does the database hold?
items.answer: A saved payment whose amount never reached the invoice credit
distractors: No payment at all, because Mongoose undoes the create on a crash
An invoice marked paid, and no payment document saved for it
A payment in a pending state that a retry job later completes
items.explanation: The payment create, the pdf update and the invoice $inc/$push are separate writes with no transaction, so a crash between them leaves a payment the invoice does not count.

items.prompt: An invoice was already soft-deleted. A second DELETE request arrives for the same id. What does invoiceController/remove.js return?
items.answer: A 404 Invoice not found, since the filter needs removed: false
distractors: A 200 again, because setting removed: true a second time is harmless
A 500, because Payment.updateMany gets a null invoice id
A 410 Gone, which marks an invoice that has been removed
items.explanation: findOneAndUpdate filters { _id, removed: false }; an already removed invoice does not match, deletedInvoice is null and the controller returns 404 before touching payments.

items.prompt: After a user logs out, an attacker replays that user's old JWT, which has not expired yet. Which check rejects the request?
items.answer: The loggedSessions check; logout pulled that token from the list
distractors: jwt.verify, as logout rotates and replaces the per-user secret
The exp claim check, as logout rewrites the token to expire now
None; the token keeps working until its own expiry time passes
items.explanation: logout.js $pulls the token from AdminPassword.loggedSessions. isValidAuthToken still verifies the signature, then rejects with 401 because loggedSessions no longer includes the token.

items.prompt: A request arrives at isValidAuthToken with an expired JWT in its Authorization header. What status does it answer with?
items.answer: A 500, since jwt.verify throws and the catch block replies
distractors: A 401 with Token verification failed, from the !verified check
A 401 with No authentication token, since it ignores the token
A 403, because an expired token is treated as forbidden
items.explanation: jsonwebtoken's verify throws TokenExpiredError rather than returning a falsy value, so the !verified branch never runs; the catch returns status 500 with jwtExpired: true. The trace table's "401 if bad" does not match the code.

items.prompt: A POST to /api/invoice/create carries a body that fails the Joi schema. Which code produces the 400 response?
items.answer: The invoice controller itself, returning before any save runs
distractors: catchErrors in errorHandlers.js, after Joi throws a ValidationError
Mongoose validators, when new Model(body).save() rejects the body
The notFound handler, which app.js registers as the final handler
items.explanation: schema.validate returns { error, value } and does not throw; create.js checks error and returns res.status(400) itself, so the request never reaches catchErrors or Mongoose.

items.prompt: Which field of each invoice record does the "paid" column in the invoice list page display?
items.answer: record.credit, the running sum of payments recorded so far
distractors: record.paymentStatus, rendered through moneyFormatter as an amount
record.total minus record.discount, the amount still owed
record.payment, the list of payment ids, shown as a count
items.explanation: The column titled translate("paid") has dataIndex: "credit" and renders it with moneyFormatter. credit is incremented by each recorded payment.

items.prompt: npm run setup crashes because the PaymentMode and Taxes model files are missing. What has it already written by then?
items.answer: The admin account and every default setting
distractors: Nothing, since setup runs in a single transaction
The Taxes default row, but not the PaymentMode row
Only the admin password, since Admin saves last
items.explanation: setup.js saves the Admin, then the AdminPassword, then Setting.insertMany, and only then requires ../models/appModels/PaymentMode and Taxes, which throws. Earlier saves stay.

items.prompt: A developer adds Product.js to backend/src/models/appModels/. How do routes such as /api/product/list come to exist?
items.answer: models/utils lists the file and appApi.js generates its routes
distractors: Someone has to add each product route to appApi.js and restart
Mongoose registers REST routes for each model it compiles
The Vite proxy creates the matching routes at build time
items.explanation: models/utils/index.js globs appModels/**/*.js and builds routesList from the file names; appApi.js loops over routesList and registers create, read, update, delete, search, list, listAll, filter and summary for each.

items.prompt: A PR drops countDocuments from the paginated list and sends count: result.length instead. What breaks?
items.answer: Page controls, because the client reads count as the total
distractors: Nothing, because result.length equals the total on every page
Sorting, because countDocuments also applied the sort order
Login, because the count query carried the admin filter
items.explanation: The list thunk builds pagination.total from data.pagination.count. result.length is only the current page, so the table thinks there is a single page.

items.prompt: A cleanup job runs Invoice.deleteMany({ removed: true }). What happens to payments that pointed at those invoices?
items.answer: Their invoice refs dangle, and autopopulate then yields null
distractors: They are deleted too, by a cascade on the invoice ref field
They are reassigned to the next invoice of the same client
Nothing, because payments copy and keep the invoice data they need
items.explanation: Payment.invoice is a ref with autopopulate: true and there is no cascade, so the hard delete leaves payments whose invoice populates as null.

items.front: In the invoice-create and login-token traces, where does a value cross the client-to-server trust boundary, and how does the server re-establish trust?
items.back: Invoice create: at the controller, Joi validates the body and the server recomputes subTotal, taxTotal and total. Auth: isValidAuthToken extracts the Bearer token, verifies its signature, and checks it is still in loggedSessions.

items.front: Where does the browser keep the IDURAR token after login, and how does it reach the server on the next request?
items.back: The auth state (with the token) is written to localStorage by the login thunk; request.js reads it and sets a default axios Authorization: Bearer <token> header.

items.front: Kata 8 caches settings in a module variable. What are its two main findings?
items.back: Blocking: no invalidation, so updateBySettingKey and the last_invoice_number bump leave stale values until restart. Important: a module-level cache is per instance and does not share across servers. Fix with a TTL (node-cache) or bust-on-write.

items.front: Why is "store the JWT in an httpOnly cookie" more than a one-line change in IDURAR?
items.back: The frontend sets the Authorization header from localStorage and isValidAuthToken reads only that header, so every call would 401. The server must read the cookie, and cookies bring CSRF risk that needs a CSRF token or SameSite.
